outcome: Extend knowledge of the world's countries using world maps, focusing on Africa, Russia, Asia (including China and India) and the Middle East.
Describe these regions' environmental zones, including polar and hot deserts, their key physical and human features, countries and major cities.
Compare the human and physical geography of a region within Africa and a region within Asia, identifying similarities, differences and links.
Explain geological timescales and plate tectonics using detailed place-based examples.
Explain rocks, weathering and soils using detailed place-based examples.
Explain weather and climate, including how climate has changed from the Ice Age to the present.
Explain glaciation, hydrology and coasts using detailed place-based examples.
Explain population change and urbanisation using place-based examples at varied scales.
Explain international development using place-based examples at varied scales.
Describe economic activity in the primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary sectors.
Explain how natural resources are used.
Explain how human and physical processes interact to change landscapes, environments and climate.
Explain how human activity depends on natural systems working effectively.
Build on knowledge of globes, maps and atlases and apply it in the classroom and the field.
Interpret Ordnance Survey maps using grid references, scale, topographic and thematic maps, and aerial and satellite photographs.
Use Geographical Information Systems to view, analyse and interpret places and data.
Carry out fieldwork in contrasting locations, collecting, analysing and drawing conclusions from complex data from multiple sources.
